questions.stem_latex:
Jo delivered catalogues as a job during her summer holidays.

She was paid a rate of \$20 per 1000 catalogues.

On an average day she delivered 4 catalogues to each residence along 45 city blocks.

Each block had on average 40 residences to receive catalogues.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: What would she have been paid for a week where she worked on 3 days?

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
It took her on average 12 minutes to cover each block.

What hourly rate of pay would be equivalent to her piecework pay rate?

questions.stem_latex:

The current share price is \$1.25 per share.

For the current year, Elysse is paid a dividend of \$0.16 per share.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: What is the current value of the shares?

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Calculate the dividend yield for the current year.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: At what annual percentage rate did the shares appreciate over the last two years?

Marnus has researched investment accounts for an amount of \$4 000, that he wishes to invest for 3 years.

His final two choices are shown below.

ACA Bank account pays compound interest at a rate of 4.9% per annum, compounded annually.

NSA Bank account pays compound interest at a rate of 4.8% per annum, compounded monthly.

How much extra will he earn over the 3 years by choosing the better option?

questions.stem_latex: Joanna has a limited budget for her holiday in the Kimberleys, so she compares all her purchases carefully. She will fly from Sydney to Broome and stay for two weeks at a resort.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Normally one-way flights from Sydney to Broome are \$1 250.

Option 1: The forward flight at a discount of 30% if she pays full price for the return flight.

Option 2: Both forward and return flights at a discount of 18%.

Which option should she choose, and why?

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
There are two resorts which she likes.

Resort A : Normal rate is \$250 per night, but a discount of 10% for bookings of a week or more.

Resort B : Normal rate is \$260 per night, but a free night is added for every six paid nights booked.

Which resort should she choose and why?

parts.label: b

The glider drifts down, losing height at a constant rate of 5 metres each second.

Draw the graph modelling the height of the glider on the grid on the previous page and determine the equation which describes the model. Label the graph Glider.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Determine the height of the glider when the stone reaches the ground.

questions.stem_latex:
When participating in a marathon, Kanye’s body typically uses 250 watts/hour.

He completed his last marathon in four and a half hours.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
How many kilowatt hours of energy did his body use in completing the marathon?

A kilowatt (kW) = 1000 watts (W).

A kilowatt hour (kWh) = 1 kilowatt consumed for an hour.

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
The body is only about 25% efficient in converting food to usable energy.

If a kilogram of pasta contains 3000 kJ of energy, how many kilograms of pasta would Kanye need to consume to give him the energy to complete the marathon.

1 Kilowatt hour (kWh) = 3600 kilojoules (kJ).

Paper typos transcribed as printed: Q10 'The graph below shown'; Q31 'measurement have been taken'; Q27 uses 'Tahliah' in table and 'Tahlia' in (b); Q27(b) dates as printed make the chat end (3:30 am Fri 20th Honolulu) before it begins (1:00 pm Sat 21st Copenhagen) - probably intended end Sat 21st (90 min); not changed, needs owner decision. Q34(c) uses a middle dot as the decimal point (0 · 615). Q36(b) text says periods between 165 and 172 months but the table shows 176 to 183 months (paper inconsistency, as printed). Q36(b) table given as cropped figure. Q22 appears before Q21 in the text layer but after it visually; ordered by number. Q24(a) grid and Q18(a) answer box are blank answer spaces; the Q24 grid is kept as a figure. Q9 option tables are cropped as option figures.
